reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
name: Schizas Grading of Lumbar Spinal Stenosis

version.label: Schizas et al. (2010), grades A1–A4, B, C, D
version.detail: Morphological grading of the dural sac on axial T2-weighted MRI, based on the rootlet/CSF ratio.

purpose: Grades the morphological severity of central lumbar spinal stenosis.

options.label: A1: Rootlets dorsal, occupying less than half of the dural sac
A2: Rootlets dorsal, contacting the dura in a horseshoe configuration
A3: Rootlets dorsal, occupying more than half of the dural sac
A4: Rootlets central, occupying most of the dural sac
B: Rootlets occupy the whole sac but CSF is still visible between them
C: No rootlets distinguishable; homogeneous grey sac without CSF; epidural fat present posteriorly
D: As C, with no posterior epidural fat visible

resultStates.label: Grade A1: no or minor stenosis
resultStates.summary: Rootlets dorsal, occupying less than half of the dural sac.

resultStates.label: Grade A2: no or minor stenosis
resultStates.summary: Rootlets dorsal, contacting the dura in a horseshoe configuration.

resultStates.label: Grade A3: no or minor stenosis
resultStates.summary: Rootlets dorsal, occupying more than half of the dural sac.

resultStates.label: Grade A4: no or minor stenosis
resultStates.summary: Rootlets central, occupying most of the dural sac.

resultStates.label: Grade B: moderate stenosis
resultStates.summary: Rootlets occupy the whole sac but CSF is still visible between them.

resultStates.label: Grade C: severe stenosis
resultStates.summary: No rootlets distinguishable; homogeneous grey sac without CSF; epidural fat present posteriorly.
resultStates.detail: Correlate with symptoms and examination; imaging severity does not determine management on its own.

resultStates.label: Grade D: extreme stenosis
resultStates.summary: As C, with no posterior epidural fat visible.
resultStates.detail: Correlate with symptoms and examination; imaging severity does not determine management on its own.

clinicalContext.text: A morphological grading that does not require measuring the canal area.

clinicalInsights.text: Grade the most stenotic level; report each level if several are affected.

limitations.text: Morphology correlates imperfectly with symptoms and walking capacity.

limitations: Lateral recess and foraminal stenosis are not graded.

confounders.effect: Supine MRI may under-show dynamic stenosis.

guideSections.what: Seven grades of central stenosis from the appearance of rootlets and CSF in the dural sac.
guideSections.howToPerform: On axial T2 at the narrowest level, assess rootlet distribution and CSF; choose the grade.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Correlate with neurogenic claudication and examination.

sources.citation: Schizas C, Theumann N, Burn A, et al. Qualitative grading of severity of lumbar spinal stenosis based on the morphology of the dural sac on magnetic resonance images. Spine. 2010;35(21):1919-1924.
